content.scenario: Rahul, a consumer, files a complaint against a company in the District Commission, Delhi, alleging that the company sold him a defective product. The company denies any wrongdoing and refuses to produce relevant documents. The District Commission wants to examine a key witness who is not willing to attend the hearing.
content.outcome: The District Commission can summon and enforce the attendance of the witness, examine the witness on oath, and require the production of relevant documents as evidence, just like a civil court would, as per Section 38(9) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
